blocks.text: But the author also wanted to make sure that the fictional story didn’t sensationalize the painful reality the show explores. “From a writing viewpoint, [it was important] knowing what to show and when to pull back and how to handle these things and being very mindful that these are not stories to be exploited,” Slaughter said. “This is something that has happened to people, and I want to make sure we’re honoring that and telling their story.”

In an exclusive featurette shared with PEOPLE, Fahy also discussed the show’s message of survival. “The show is really heavy but it’s so hopeful,” she said. “Ultimately I think [what] we’re hoping to take away is your trauma really doesn’t define you if you don’t let it.” All episodes of The Good Daughter premiere on Peacock on Nov. 12.

blocks.text: ⟦1⟧’s 2017 crime thriller, ⟦2⟧, is getting a TV adaptation. The author and executive producer wanted the more disturbing parts of the book to come across carefully on screen. The author, 55, talked about turning the book into a series at an early screening of The Good Daughter in New York City on Oct. 29, hosted by Peacock and People Who Read. The Good Daughter, which stars ⟦3⟧ and ⟦4⟧, follows sisters Charlotte “Charlie” and Samantha “Sam” Quinn. Their lives change after their family is hit by a brutal act of violence. Years later, another shocking event hits their small town. Charlie, now a lawyer like her father, becomes an important witness in another tragedy.

Slaughter serves as a showrunner and an executive producer on the series, and also wrote all six episodes with director Steph Green. It was Slaughter’s first stint as a screenwriter, and she paid special attention to certain elements of the book — particularly the story’s heavier elements.

“It started before we even shot anything,” Slaughter told PEOPLE’s senior books editor Lizz Schumer during the event’s Q&A. “One of the deeper conversations I had before we signed on Steph Green, the director, who did such a wonderful job, was ‘How are we going to protect everybody on set, because we’re dealing with these heavy things?’” Slaughter says the crew was also “very protective” of child actors Drew Cheek and Audrey Grace Marshall, who play younger versions of Charlie and Sam.

Need your next page-turner? See which books our editors can’t put down with ⟦1⟧ — plus get PEOPLE News.

“Normally I hate children, and babies in particular. They’re just so boneless and bewildered when they come out,” Slaughter jokes. “But these kids were great. … We just were so careful to make sure everybody felt protected.” As such, Slaughter made sure there were intimacy coordinators and a mental health expert on set. They also used body doubles while shooting some of the more intense scenes, so the child actresses “weren’t actually in these situations” themselves.
